note: fork F4D -- THE FIFTH BASELINE: CONFIGURATION (1), the shipped configuration in which libmh.dll is NOT beside mh.dll and the 627-TU spine is therefore not in the process at all (ruling Q10, ratified). RECORDED FROM THE FIRST CONFIG-(1) BOOT THAT HAS EVER HAPPENED -- before F4D the spine could not be absent, because it was compiled in. THIS IS NOT A VARIANT OF `original`, and reading it as one would be the mistake worth naming: `[config] mode=original` is a run that HAS the spine and declines to promote from it, so its arm still emits the [rebind] block and the [promote] domain reports (which is why that baseline is 44 steps and this one is 40). Configuration (1) has no spine to ask. IT IS ALSO KEYED DIFFERENTLY, by necessity: `[config mode=...]` is printed by mh::rebind::report_arming, a LIBMH row, so the line that names the mode is one of the lines the missing module takes with it. check_arm_order's CONFIG1_RE anchors on the bind's own outcome line instead -- a statement about what the arm DID, emitted by mh.dll, which is the same move F4B made when it re-pointed NOMODULE_RE onto the banner. ONE REFUSAL OUTCOME IS TEMPLATED HERE AND TWO DELIBERATELY ARE NOT -- see step #2's `why`. `NOT BOUND` (the file is simply not there) is the SHIPPED configuration and is templated. `LOADED BUT REFUSED` and `ABI MISMATCH` are broken deployments, and their lines name the symbols or the numbers that disagreed -- a build-specific list no template can mask into a stable string. They are gated by tools/check_module_bind.py --libmh, which classifies all three outcomes by name and is the tool that owns the bind verdict; this file owns ORDER. Edit ONLY with a --compare verdict in the same commit saying which steps moved and why.

; [modules] libmh: NOT BOUND -- LoadLibrary(<PATH>) failed, Win<N> error <N> (the file is not there). This run is CONFIGURATION (<N>): mh.dll does not contain the spine, so the game runs the original binary's own bodies. Nothing is promoted and nothing is instrumented; that is the configuration, not a failure of the boot.
lines.why: THE KEY LINE of this baseline: CONFIG1_RE reads the baseline key off it, because the usual key -- `[config mode=...]` -- is printed by mh::rebind::report_arming, which is a LIBMH row and therefore one of the lines the missing module takes with it. TEMPLATED FOR THE SHIPPED SHAPE ONLY. The bind has three refusal outcomes and all three leave the same process running the same original bodies, but only this one is a configuration somebody ships: `LOADED BUT REFUSED` names the contract symbols that did not resolve and `ABI MISMATCH` names two struct sizes, and neither list can be masked into a string a baseline can hold. So the other two select this key (that is what CONFIG1_RE matches) and then RED here, loudly, at this step -- which is the right answer for a broken deployment, and is exactly what a live f4d_wrong lane (mh_net.dll planted under the name libmh.dll) produced when this was measured. check_module_bind --libmh is what tells the three apart by name.

alt: ; [modules] mh_harness: NOT BOUND -- LoadLibrary(<PATH>) failed, Win<N> error <N> (the file is not there). This run is UNINSTRUMENTED: no per-step hashes, no journal, no determinism log. The game is unaffected -- the harness only observes -- so the boot continues.

lines.why: INSERTED BY fork F4E, and it is the item's ONE ruled baseline edit -- the THIRD member of the class F4A pre-ruled at ruling (b): a satellite bound from DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH costs exactly one structural line at the head of the window. This one is mh_harness.dll, the determinism/replay INSTRUMENT -- seams/harness.cpp, 8.3k lines, which used to be mh.dll's single largest file. VERDICT THAT AUTHORISED IT (check_arm_order --compare, the pre-F4E run of the same mode -> the F4E run): 1 structural edit, 0 text changes, and NOTHING ELSE MOVED -- measured on all four committed templates (brokered 70->71, original 44->45, brokered_nomodule 72->73, config1 40->41). It is ONE line and not two on purpose, the same constraint both sibling binds state: the loader-order fact and the two row counts are folded into this line rather than printed separately, so the bound and absent arms are structurally identical and cost one step each. The row counts (host=27/27 spine=30/30) are the item's own evidence: host rows resolve out of mh.dll and spine rows out of libmh.dll, and `spine=0/30` is Q4's refusal stated in numbers -- configuration (1) with the instrument declining to arm rather than reading invented state. IT GOES LAST OF THE THREE BINDS, and that IS a contract (see mh.c): the instrument is handed libmh's bind verdict as an argument, so it cannot be bound before libmh has been. -- ALT (fork F4E): the same step as read on a lane with NO mh_harness.dll. Absence of the instrument is not a different ARM -- it is the same thirteen shims answering what the un-armed bodies already answered -- so it is an alternative spelling of this step rather than a fifth template. The registered `harness_absent` scenario is the lane that reads it. The `call-through ok` clause is not decoration and is required by tools/check_module_bind.py: GetProcAddress succeeding is not evidence that a CALL across the boundary works, and neither is the module's init returning its ABI (that is a call into the module-level entry, not into the contract). The probe is MH_Harness_WantsPresentTick, chosen for the three reasons MH_Net_IsStarted is one module over -- pure, no side effect, and a KNOWN answer at DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH (0, because load_config has not run).
